From: Aisha Desai <aisha.desai@rapidretail.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:02:11 -0700
Subject: Spike: 99th pct latency and elevated 5xxs impacting checkout

Jonas —

We hit a significant degradation on checkout starting ~08:30 PT this morning. 99th percentile latency climbed from ~350ms to >3.2s, and we saw a sustained 1.8% 5xx rate for ~40 minutes. This impacted checkout completion for several enterprise customers (order volume ~peak). Our ops team partially mitigated by rolling traffic off the region but revenue impact was visible.

Can you confirm (a) root cause, (b) immediate corrective actions, and (c) what exec-level remediation and credits we should expect? Our EMEA execs are asking for an ASAP briefing.

We need a formal RCA and an executive summary we can share with procurement and finance. Attaching the alert timeline from our side.

— Aisha
Aisha Desai
Head of Platform, RapidRetail

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 11:54:02 -07:00
Subject: DRAFT RCA (RapidRetail) + immediate corrective actions

Jonas —

High-level summary (draft):
- Timeline: 08:27 PT — Traffic pattern shift observed; 08:30 — 5xx increase and 99p latency spike; 09:12 — partial traffic re-route to backup pool; 09:42 — nominal levels restored.
- Root cause (primary): A sudden workload skew caused cache-miss amplification on the checkout path. The KV-cache policy for the relevant model shard (in region us-west-2) was evicting prefixes due to an atypical request distribution; this combined with a short-lived kernel selection fallback to a scalar path on the GPU runtime, increasing per-token CPU use and queuing latency.
- Contributing factors: the autoscaler decision window was too coarse (120s) for this workload burst; there was no preconfigured prefix-level hot-keying for this tenant; the A/B fallback policy returned a heavier execution kernel when memory pressure spiked.

Immediate corrective actions taken (during incident):
1) Manual traffic diversion to dedicated pool for RapidRetail at 09:12. (Owner: SRE runbook, Ben)
2) Forced prefix cache pinning for the active checkout prefixes for the tenant (temporary config) at 09:20. (Owner: runtime ops)
3) Shortened decision window on the HPA to 30s for the affected pool as a hotfix. (Owner: infra)

Planned remediation (proposed owners & ETA):
- Short-term (7 days):
  - Persist prefix pinning capability and add a tenant-level toggle in console (Owner: runtime, ETA: 2028-08-21)
  - Add a hot-key detection rule to pre-warm KV cache for high-volume prefixes (Owner: serving/runtime, ETA: 2028-08-20)
  - Reduce autoscaler decision window configurable per pool and add a monitoring alert (Owner: infra, ETA: 2028-08-19)
- Medium-term (30 days):
  - Kernel selection safeguard: prevent fallback to scalar execution under memory-pressure scenarios for high-SLA routes (Owner: runtime engineering, ETA: 2028-09-13)
  - Enhanced load-testing scenarios to include sudden skew and hot-key amplification tests (Owner: QE, ETA: 2028-09-11)

Proposed customer remediation:
- Service credit proposal: 10% of committed monthly usage for the affected billing period, pending legal/finance signoff. (Owner: Accounts/Finance)
- Joint post-incident review session with RapidRetail engineering + our runtime leads; propose 45-minute readout.

Attachments included: rapidretail_rca_v1.pdf (detailed traces + timelines), service-metrics-20280814.csv (aggregated metrics), initial-stack-trace.txt

Notes: This draft needs the executive summary tightened (one-pager) and approval on the credit amount before we go external.

— Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, procurement@rapidretail.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 14:05:45 -07:00
Subject: RapidRetail incident: executive summary and next steps

Aisha —

Thanks for flagging this and for the alert snapshot. We appreciate the urgency. Please find a concise executive summary below (we will attach Ben's full RCA for engineering review):

Executive summary (one-paragraph): On 2028-08-14 at ~08:30 PT, RapidRetail experienced elevated checkout latency and a brief increase in 5xx errors due to a cache-miss amplification combined with a temporary fallback to a higher-latency execution kernel in our serving runtime. Our team diverted traffic and pinned hot prefixes to a dedicated pool, restoring service within ~45 minutes. We propose short-term controls (configurable prefix pinning, autoscaler window tuning) and medium-term runtime safeguards to reduce recurrence risk.

Proposed customer remediation and ask:
- We recommend a 10% service credit for the billing period as a good-faith remediation; finance/legal needs to sign off.
- We will run a joint post-incident review (45 minutes) this week. Please share preferred windows.

Planned next steps (internal):
- Ben to finalize RCA and confirm ETAs on the remediation items.
- Grace to confirm the exact config changes made during the incident and update runbook.
- Jonas to run the executive readout and provide the one-pager.

We have attached the detailed RCA for your engineering team. 

Attachments: rapidretail_rca_v1.pdf

Thanks,

— Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
